set.title: ESAT Chemistry — First 10
set.authorship: Original questions informed by the official 2026–27 ESAT Chemistry specification, the official Chemistry guide, and the style of historic NSAA Chemistry papers. No question has been copied.
providedDataPolicy: Every relative atomic mass needed for a calculation is supplied in the question.
Atomic numbers, electron counts, molar gas volumes and specific heat capacities are supplied whenever required.
No question requires the user to consult a periodic table.
Questions may still test specification knowledge such as ionic bonding, electrolysis products and common chemical formulae.
researchBasis: Official format: 27 multiple-choice questions in 40 minutes, computer-based and non-calculator.
Chemistry assumes the Chemistry specification plus Mathematics 1 knowledge.
Historic NSAA Chemistry sections repeatedly use short multi-stage calculations, data tables, graphs, chromatography, balanced equations, equilibrium and occasional statement-combination questions.
Only one of these ten questions uses the statement-combination format to preserve variety.
set.displayOrderPurpose: Retention-optimised order: a solvable but non-trivial opening, early visual variety, alternating conceptual and quantitative styles, then three increasingly layered capstone questions.

questions.stemMarkdown:
\(20.0\text{ cm}^3\) of \(0.50\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\) calcium chloride solution is mixed with \(30.0\text{ cm}^3\) of \(0.40\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\) silver nitrate solution.

Silver ions and chloride ions react completely according to

\[\mathrm{Ag^+(aq)+Cl^-(aq)\rightarrow AgCl(s)}.\]

How many moles of chloride ions remain in the mixture?

solution.title: Count chloride ions before comparing them with silver ions.
stepsMarkdown: Moles of \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}=0.0200\times0.50=0.0100\).
Each mole of \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}\) supplies two moles of \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\), so there are \(0.0200\) mol of chloride ions.
Moles of \(\mathrm{Ag^+}=0.0300\times0.40=0.0120\).
The reaction is 1:1, so chloride remaining is \(0.0200-0.0120=0.0080\) mol.

distractorMap.reason: Subtracts the moles of calcium chloride from the moles of silver ions.
Halves the correct excess chloride amount.
Correct.
Uses the moles of calcium chloride without accounting for two chloride ions per formula unit.
Gives the initial amount of silver ions rather than the chloride left over.
Gives the initial amount of chloride and ignores the precipitation reaction.

questions.stemMarkdown:
A sample containing exactly two substances is separated by paper chromatography. The ruler readings are shown in the diagram.

The possible substances have the following \(R_f\) values:

| Substance | P | Q | R | S | T |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| \(R_f\) | 0.25 | 0.40 | 0.50 | 0.70 | 0.75 |

Which two substances are present in the sample?

solution.title: Measure every distance from the baseline, not from zero on the ruler.
stepsMarkdown: The solvent moves from \(1.0\) cm to \(11.0\) cm, so its distance is \(10.0\) cm.
The lower spot moves \(5.0-1.0=4.0\) cm, giving \(R_f=4.0/10.0=0.40\).
The upper spot moves \(8.5-1.0=7.5\) cm, giving \(R_f=7.5/10.0=0.75\).
These correspond to Q and T.

distractorMap.reason: Uses the lower spot correctly but treats the upper ruler reading as its travel distance.
Uses an incorrect lower-spot distance but identifies the upper spot correctly.
Uses the lower ruler reading directly and rounds the upper result down.
Correct.
Measures both spot positions from zero on the ruler.
Rounds both calculated values upward to nearby table entries.

questions.stemMarkdown:
A monatomic ion \(X^{2-}\) contains 18 electrons.

Element \(X\) has two isotopes, \(^{32}X\) and \(^{34}X\). The abundance of \(^{32}X\) is \(90\%\).

Which row gives the electron configuration of an atom of \(X\) and the relative atomic mass of \(X\)?

solution.title: Remove the two extra electrons before finding the atomic configuration.
stepsMarkdown: The \(2-\) ion has gained two electrons, so a neutral atom has \(18-2=16\) electrons.
Its electron configuration is therefore \(2,8,6\).
The weighted mean is \((32\times0.90)+(34\times0.10)=32.2\).

distractorMap.reason: Removes four electrons from the ion instead of two.
Correct.
Uses the electron configuration of the ion rather than the atom.
Reverses the isotope abundances.
Uses both the ion configuration and reversed abundances.
Uses the mass number of the heavier isotope as the relative atomic mass.

questions.stemMarkdown:
\(0.800\text{ g}\) of a fuel is burned beneath \(200\text{ g}\) of water. The water temperature rises by \(12.0\,^{\circ}\text{C}\).

Only \(75\%\) of the energy released by the fuel is transferred to the water.

The relative molar mass of the fuel is \(32.0\), and the specific heat capacity of water is \(4.0\text{ J g}^{-1}\,^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}\).

What is the magnitude of the energy released per mole of fuel?

solution.title: The water receives only three quarters of the released energy.
stepsMarkdown: Energy gained by water: \(q=mc\Delta T=200\times4.0\times12.0=9600\text{ J}=9.6\text{ kJ}\).
Energy released by the fuel sample: \(9.6/0.75=12.8\text{ kJ}\).
Moles of fuel: \(0.800/32.0=0.0250\text{ mol}\).
Energy per mole: \(12.8/0.0250=512\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).

distractorMap.reason: Multiplies the water's energy gain by 75% instead of correcting for the lost energy.
Treats the water's energy gain as the full energy released.
Uses an incorrect fuel amount of \(0.020\) mol.
Correct.
Uses the efficiency correction in the wrong place and rounds prematurely.
Treats the 75% transfer as though only half the released energy reached the water.

questions.stemMarkdown:
Magnesium reacts with excess hydrochloric acid according to

\[\mathrm{Mg(s)+2HCl(aq)\rightarrow MgCl_2(aq)+H_2(g)}.\]

The graph shows the volume of hydrogen collected.

At the conditions used, one mole of gas occupies \(24\text{ dm}^3\).

What is the average rate of consumption of hydrochloric acid during the first \(20\text{ s}\)?

solution.title: Convert the gas volume to moles, then use the reaction ratio.
stepsMarkdown: At \(20\text{ s}\), \(96\text{ cm}^3=0.096\text{ dm}^3\) of hydrogen has formed.
Twice as many moles of HCl are consumed, so \(0.0080\) mol of HCl reacts.
Average rate: \(0.0080/20=4.0\times10^{-4}\text{ mol s}^{-1}\).

distractorMap.reason: Calculates the hydrogen-production rate but does not apply the 2:1 HCl-to-hydrogen ratio.
Correct.
Applies the 2:1 ratio twice.
Converts cubic centimetres to cubic decimetres by a factor of 100 rather than 1000.
Combines the unit-conversion error with an extra factor of two.
Uses the gas volume directly as though it were an amount in moles.

questions.stemMarkdown:
Molten aluminium oxide is electrolysed using inert electrodes. \(5.4\text{ g}\) of aluminium is produced.

What volume of oxygen is produced at room temperature and pressure?

\[A_r(\mathrm{Al})=27\]
One mole of gas occupies \(24\text{ dm}^3\) at room temperature and pressure.

solution.title: Use the aluminium-to-oxygen ratio from aluminium oxide.
stepsMarkdown: The overall change is \(2\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\rightarrow4\mathrm{Al}+3\mathrm{O_2}\).
Moles of aluminium: \(5.4/27=0.20\).
Moles of oxygen: \(0.20\times\dfrac34=0.15\).
Volume: \(0.15\times24=3.6\text{ dm}^3\).

distractorMap.reason: Uses an oxygen-to-aluminium ratio of 1:4.
Uses an oxygen-to-aluminium ratio of 1:2.
Correct.
Assumes equal moles of aluminium and oxygen.
Uses the formula subscripts as a 3:2 oxygen-to-aluminium ratio.
Uses twice as many moles of oxygen as aluminium.

questions.stemMarkdown: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

statementItems.textMarkdown: Molten sodium chloride conducts electricity because its ions are free to move.
Graphite conducts electricity because it contains delocalised electrons that can move through the structure.
When bromine boils, the covalent bonds within \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) molecules are broken.

solution.title: Distinguish mobile charged particles from bonds inside molecules.
stepsMarkdown: 1 is true: molten ionic compounds contain mobile ions.
2 is true: graphite has mobile delocalised electrons.
3 is false: boiling overcomes intermolecular forces between bromine molecules, not the covalent bond inside each molecule.

distractorMap.reason: Statements 1 and 2 are both true.
Misses the mobile electrons in graphite.
Misses the mobile ions in molten sodium chloride.
Statement 3 confuses intermolecular forces with covalent bonds.
Correct.
Includes the false statement 3 and misses statement 2.
Includes the false statement 3 and misses statement 1.
Statement 3 is false.

questions.stemMarkdown:
Sulfur dioxide and oxygen reach equilibrium according to

\[\mathrm{2SO_2(g)+O_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2SO_3(g)}.\]

Initially, the mixture contains \(4.0\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) and \(3.0\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\), with no \(\mathrm{SO_3}\).

At equilibrium, \(75\%\) of the original sulfur dioxide has been converted into sulfur trioxide. At this temperature and pressure, one mole of gas occupies \(30.0\text{ dm}^3\).

What is the total volume of the equilibrium mixture?

solution.title: Find every equilibrium amount before adding the gas moles.
stepsMarkdown: \(75\%\) of \(4.0\) mol means \(3.0\) mol of \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) reacts.
This consumes \(1.5\) mol of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) and forms \(3.0\) mol of \(\mathrm{SO_3}\).
Equilibrium amounts are \(1.0\), \(1.5\), and \(3.0\) mol, giving \(5.5\) mol in total.
Volume: \(5.5\times30.0=165\text{ dm}^3\).

distractorMap.reason: Counts only the sulfur trioxide formed.
Counts the unreacted gases but omits the sulfur trioxide.
Rounds the total amount to 5 mol.
Correct.
Assumes the equilibrium mixture contains 6 mol in total.
Uses the initial total amount of 7 mol and ignores the reduction in gas moles.

questions.stemMarkdown:
\(100\text{ cm}^3\) of a gaseous hydrocarbon \(X\) is mixed with \(700\text{ cm}^3\) of oxygen and burned completely.

After the products are cooled to the original temperature, all the water is liquid and the remaining gases occupy \(500\text{ cm}^3\).

The carbon dioxide is then completely removed. The gas left occupies \(200\text{ cm}^3\) and is oxygen.

All gas volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure.

What is the molecular formula of \(X\)?

solution.title: Use the carbon dioxide volume first, then the oxygen consumed.
stepsMarkdown: The carbon dioxide volume is \(500-200=300\text{ cm}^3\).
So each volume of hydrocarbon forms three equal volumes of carbon dioxide: \(X\) contains three carbon atoms.
Oxygen consumed is \(700-200=500\text{ cm}^3\), or five volumes per volume of hydrocarbon.
For \(\mathrm{C_3H_y}\), complete combustion needs \(3+y/4=5\) moles of oxygen, so \(y=8\).

distractorMap.reason: Uses the final oxygen volume to infer the carbon count.
Finds two carbon atoms by ignoring the carbon dioxide removed.
Finds three carbon atoms but assumes the hydrocarbon is an alkene.
Correct.
Treats the total gas remaining after cooling as carbon dioxide.
Infers four carbon atoms and then assumes an alkane.

questions.stemMarkdown:
An antacid tablet contains magnesium hydroxide and an inert filler.

The tablet is added to \(30.0\text{ cm}^3\) of \(0.500\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\) hydrochloric acid, which is in excess. After the reaction is complete, the excess hydrochloric acid is exactly neutralised by \(10.0\text{ cm}^3\) of \(0.300\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\) sodium hydroxide.

\[\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2+2HCl\rightarrow MgCl_2+2H_2O}\]

The relative molar mass of \(\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}\) is \(58.0\).

What mass of magnesium hydroxide was present in the tablet?

solution.title: Use the second titration to find how much acid was left over.
stepsMarkdown: Initial HCl: \(0.0300\times0.500=0.0150\) mol.
Excess HCl: \(0.0100\times0.300=0.0030\) mol, because HCl and NaOH react 1:1.
HCl that reacted with the tablet: \(0.0150-0.0030=0.0120\) mol.

distractorMap.reason: Uses only the excess acid and then applies the 2:1 ratio.
Divides the acid consumed by four instead of two.
Correct.
Assumes all the original acid reacted with magnesium hydroxide but otherwise uses the correct 2:1 ratio.
Uses a 1:1 ratio between HCl and magnesium hydroxide.
Uses all the initial acid and also assumes a 1:1 ratio.
